verse: I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Marvelous are Your works, and I know this very well.
story: David has just spent thirteen verses admitting that God knows him completely, and his answer is not fear but praise.

Fearfully and wonderfully made points back to the womb, where, the psalm says, God knit him together. The words carry awe: David stands before his own body as before a work of careful craft, and he gives the credit to the Maker. He does not say he is impressive. He says God's works are marvelous, and that his own soul knows it well. Being known through and through, by the One who made us, turns out to be a reason to worship and not to hide.
Thank Him today for the person He made you, body and mind, just as you are. Praise is a good place to begin.
